index_title: OLD idempotent boundary certificates, forest pruning and bounded hidden obstructions
scope: Private B058: all SIX source16 results, TWO equations, eleven definitions, 74 human claims and eight tasks. Literal OLD coordinate certificates survive deletion of idempotent gaps. A finite typed positive semigroup has no zero on actual composable intervals; a published factorisation-forest input bounds height. Keep first/last children and STOP recursion in deleted middle intervals, producing a disjoint partition of the ORIGINAL branch words. One complete old base and simultaneous whole-word insertion reconstruct the original simple bad cycle. Therefore UNARY-ADMISSIBLE noncompletable partial hidden inputs have bounded OLD closed obstructions. The forest theorem adds one explicit receiving obligation to the five existing HN/HKN bindings; no compiled provider is claimed.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. OLD source terms remain literal after induced restriction; target coincidences are never source seams. Idempotent diversity e is not reflexive: its RAW envelope is E_e=Id union e. Actual distinct representatives are needed before extracting a fine atom in e.

assumptions.statement: Every strict FULL invariant cover on every old real sort has infinite relative index, including Top covers. This supplies the terminal named proper-coordinate providers; exact MI reconstruction of an idempotent envelope retains its separately proved exactness/lattice premises.

assumptions.statement: Actual real and proper nonzero represented MI quotient sorts have the finite named unary projections, upward maps and quotient transitions/inverses and complete semantic cylinders. Functions are actual equivariant maps, with no quotient-to-real or nullary vertex generators. No extra non-MI quotient is added.

assumptions.statement: C is finite and functionally closed; every FULL one-generated induced diagram is an actual completed hidden member. Thus its singleton closures have the uniform m_typ bound and satisfy all actual unary identities. C as a whole need not be completable.

assumptions.name: Locally vetted OLD supported macro path
assumptions.statement: For the boundary/path applications, all actual joined irreducible one-/two-root source supports have passed the full local induced-pattern test. Old vertices b_0,...,b_n are pairwise distinct formal source roots, n>=1; each macro P_i is the positive STRONG profile of the EXACT original traversed branch word w_i, with its nonempty original pair menu D_i subset P_i. Only genuine OLD source endpoint pairs issue sides.

assumptions.name: Conditional reconstruction base and anchor
assumptions.statement: For reconstruction, A is one finite COMPLETE old base containing distinct chosen representatives of ALL retained old roots. Retained side atoms lie in their original P_i; every deleted-gap pair lies in E_e=Id union e. The fixed ORIGINAL anchor word has its endpoint atom in its OWN strong profile. This last condition is explicit, not inferred from unrelated retained sides.

assumptions.name: Given valid ordered forest for structural pruning
assumptions.statement: For the combinatorial partition branch a finite ordered tree has macro-letter leaves in their original order and contiguous interval nodes, no unary internal nodes; each internal node with at least three children has the SAME idempotent nonzero value on all its children. This is a supplied finite tree; its existence/height bound is a separate E01 application.

assumptions.name: Separate optional higher-support gate
assumptions.statement: All six results are prepared in the BINARY hidden setting. A finite-arity reading requires its separate support-normal complete frozen-factor completion/reflection interface. Binary SAP/word injection alone does not preserve old arity>=3 factor tuples.

external_providers.name: Finite-semigroup factorisation forest height
external_providers.source_version: Kufleitner, MFCS 2008, LNCS 5162, The Height of Factorization Forests
external_providers.theorem: Theorem 1; use the weaker height bound 3|S| proved explicitly
external_providers.statement: For any finite semigroup S and evaluation homomorphism from nonempty words, each word admits an ordered factorisation tree of height at most 3|S| (leaves at height zero). Internal nodes have at least two children; at arity at least three every child has the same idempotent image. The pinned existing Lean declaration supplies the stronger 3|S|-1 bound. Its independent receiving build/axiom audit and adapter to the finite typed positive semigroup remain pending; see formalization/FACTORIZATION_FOREST_PROVIDER.md.

lean_reference.representation: General finite nonempty semigroup, arbitrary alphabet, nonempty-list multiplicative evaluation; ordered factorization tree with exact original yield, leaves height0, no unary nodes and wide common-idempotent children; height <= 3*card(S)-1.

definitions.statement: S_typ is{0} disjoint union of all nonempty typed reachable profiles, retaining endpoint sort tags. Noncomposable factors multiply to zero; zero absorbs. No STRONG identity unit is adjoined.

definitions.statement: For nonempty same-sort e with e*e=e, E_e=Id union e is the FULL RAW exact envelope. e itself is irreflexive and is not an equivalence relation.

definitions.name: Maximal stopped gap
definitions.statement: At a node with>=3 common-idempotent children, keep first/last subtrees, record the ENTIRE intervening original interval once and STOP recursion inside it. Record its original words and boundary roots.

definitions.statement: One ORIGINAL whole atomic private branch of the bad cycle is retained separately. Its two OLD root endpoints and complete old pair support are retained; its exact word endpoint profile must be admissible in A.

claims.name: Typed bounded hidden obstruction source export
claims.statement: Every noncompletable UNARY-ADMISSIBLE finite functionally closed partial C has an induced closed noncompletable OLD substructure of size<=N_typ by C46-C57. This is the binary theorem; the finite-arity variant remains separately conditional on A10.

claims.name: Completion coincidences cannot create a deleted-gap seam
claims.statement: A reducible source may identify two distinct old vertices in a HE target. Replacing them by a common intermediate term would add an OLD equation not present in C. C11-C14 compose only literal source terms and then restrict them; target equality plays no role.

claims.name: Do not replace an idempotent envelope by the SAP monolith
claims.statement: Even if e lies above the least strong idempotent, its valid gap certificate only forces E_e=Id union e. It does not force the generally finer monolith L. The reconstruction uses exactly E_e and e, never an unsupported L-equality.

claims.name: A formal diversity palette is never a reflexive equivalence
claims.statement: Nonempty e consists of irreflexive same-sort atoms. The RAW envelope E_e separately includes actual Id; membership in it becomes a diversity atom in e ONLY after distinct representatives. Omitting this distinction would invalidate gap reconstruction.

claims.name: Never recurse into a recorded deleted middle interval
claims.statement: If deletion were recorded both at a wide ancestor and inside its discarded child, the records would overlap and count original macro edges more than once. C21 explicitly stops recursion there, which is essential for C22 exact partition and C39 simple reconstruction.

claims.name: Retained root counts may be twice the leaf count
claims.statement: Deleted gaps can separate retained letters, so their endpoints need not form one consecutive path. Count at most two OLD roots per retained letter, including both gap boundaries; leafcount+1 can be too small. No completion vertex is introduced to close the count.

claims.name: The fixed anchor hypothesis cannot be dropped
claims.statement: Endpoint atoms allowed for the complementary retained path and deleted gaps may fail the fixed anchor profile. C37/C54 retain and discharge this independent requirement; C38 would not otherwise reconstruct the original bad cycle.

claims.name: Whole ORIGINAL words are required, not interchangeable profiles
claims.statement: A profile can have several different atomic word presentations. Substituting another word with the same value might realize a different cycle and yield no contradiction to the original bad specified cycle. C25/C35 preserve exact original sequences.

claims.name: One common base is needed for all insertions
claims.statement: Independently chosen realizations could assign incompatible old pair colours or collide new interiors. I13/C38 use ONE already complete base and preserve all of it, while cross colours between newly inserted distinct interiors remain freely whatever the old SAP amalgam supplies.

claims.name: Arbitrary total-unary partial sources invalidate the uniform bound
claims.statement: Long malformed inverse-transition cycles are one-generated irreducible and noncompletable, with no proper nonempty closed substructure. They fail A06. Therefore no fixed N_typ can be claimed for all finite total-unary partial inputs.

claims.name: The forest theorem is an exposed external receiving obligation
claims.statement: E01 is the precise published finite-semigroup height input already cited by the manuscript, newly made explicit in this package. No verified Lean declaration/encoding adapter is asserted. It adds ONE forest receiving obligation to the unchanged THREE HN and TWO HKN obligations; total six.

claims.name: The literal 2007 citation has a monoid/semigroup wording issue
claims.statement: The source bibliography cites arxiv0710.5130, whose abstract uses finite semigroups but displayed theorem says finite monoids. E01 uses the later2008 finite-SEMIGROUP Theorem1, retaining the needed weaker3|S| bound. The typed zero completion need not have a global unit, so blindly applying a monoid-only API would be invalid or change the bound.

claims.name: Finite diagnostics do not prove the published forest theorem
claims.statement: The controls enumerate bounded valid trees and small semigroup words, verify stopped-gap partition, exact original labels, OLD boundary persistence, source-term transport and finite simple-cycle assembly. They do not prove arbitrary forest existence/height or infinite SAP/CCO. E01 remains external.

claims.name: Higher-support realization keeps its separate interface
claims.statement: Binary pair reflection and original SAP injection reconstruct only binary old diagrams. A conditional higher-arity conclusion must retain complete old higher-support factors and the separate support-normal preservation/reflection premise A10; it is not proved from pair shadows.

claims.name: Empty represented MI families and short paths are covered
claims.statement: When E_e=Top, C16 uses an empty equality family. A one-letter macro path needs no deletion and a height0 leaf has retained endpoints. Binary forest nodes and wide nodes with k=3 (one middle child) satisfy the same partition induction. No empty original macro word is assumed.

claims.name: Induced OLD restriction is not itself a completion
claims.statement: The support C45 can remain partial and noncompletable; that is the intended conclusion C56. Its source literals persist under induced restriction, without filling absent relations or assuming global C has a completion to construct the certificate.

claims.name: Earlier source qualifications and public boundaries remain
claims.statement: All frozen TeX hashes remain unchanged; the TV1 guarded/RAW repair is retained in the B057 provider and no false full RAW equality for diversity D is used here. Earlier B047 actual/FULL-sector and B048 higher-support gates remain. This is private human preparation, not Lean/global certification, and public Work/CI/policy remain untouched.
